1.title: Strip both wire ends bare
1.say: Lay the two white wires apart on the table in front of you. Strip about one centimetre of coating off each wire tip with the blue stripping tool.
placements: first white wire tip → about one centimetre inside blue and red stripping tool jaws to cut outer coating, in the video: right hand wire over blue table
second white wire tip → about one centimetre inside blue and red stripping tool jaws to cut outer coating, in the video: left hand wire over blue table
watch_for: if copper strands look cut or missing, you squeezed too hard or stripped more than about one centimetre
if coating still covers the tip, the tool did not pull cleanly so strip again
1.check_yourself: It should look like two white wires lying apart with short shiny copper ends exposed.
1.safety: Keep your fingers clear of the stripping tool jaws when you squeeze.

2.title: Twist bare ends together
2.say: Hold one white wire in each hand with the copper tips touching end to end. Twist the two copper tips around each other to lock them tight.
placements: two bare copper ends → pushed end to end then twisted around each other at middle of loop, in the video: bottom centre of white wire circle on blue table
watch_for: if the join pulls apart with a light tug, the copper ends were not twisted tight enough
if sharp copper points stick out, twist them flat or they will poke through the tube
2.check_yourself: It should look like one white wire loop with copper ends twisted into a small neat join.

3.title: Spread flux on twisted join
3.say: Hold the white wire loop steady with one hand. Dab a little flux paste onto the twisted copper join with the small black stick.
placements: flux paste → dabbed with thin black stick to cover whole twisted copper join in middle of white loop, in the video: bottom centre of loop on blue table
watch_for: if dry copper still shows, you missed a spot so add a little more flux to the join
if thick blobs drip off, you used too much flux so wipe the extra away
3.check_yourself: It should look like the twisted copper join looks wet and shiny in the middle of the white loop.

4.title: Melt solder onto the join
4.say: Hold the hot soldering iron tip against the white wire copper join. Touch the thin silver solder wire to the join until it melts and spreads.
placements: hot soldering iron tip preloaded with solder → pressed against twisted copper join at middle of white wire loop, in the video: iron comes down from top centre
thin silver solder wire → touched to hot join until melted silver spreads along copper, in the video: fed from right hand
watch_for: if solder balls up and will not spread, the join is not hot enough so hold the iron longer
if the white coating melts back, the iron was on too long or too close to the coating
4.check_yourself: It should look like the centre join is covered with smooth shiny silver solder between the white wires.
4.safety: Never touch the hot iron tip and hold the wire well back from the heat.

5.title: Slide tube over the join
5.say: Pick up the short black tube with one hand. Slide the tube over the white wire and centre it on the join.
placements: short black shrink tube → threaded onto one white wire end then slid to middle to cover whole silver join, in the video: bottom centre of loop with white showing both sides
watch_for: if bare silver or copper still shows at either end, the tube is off centre so slide it to cover
if the tube is loose and slides freely, it is too wide so use a shorter snug tube
5.check_yourself: It should look like a black tube covers the soldered join with white coating visible on both sides.

6.title: Heat sleeve tight around join
6.say: Hold the white wire steady well back from the black tube. Aim the hot gun nozzle at the tube and sweep gently until it shrinks tight.
placements: hot gun silver nozzle → held just above black tube at middle of white wire loop and swept gently along tube, in the video: nozzle from top left over blue table
watch_for: if the tube still slides loosely, it is not hot enough so warm it a little longer
if the white coating bubbles or browns, you overheated it so lift the heat away sooner
6.check_yourself: It should look like the black sleeve is shrunk tight around the white wire with no bare metal showing.
6.safety: Keep your fingers clear of the hot air and do not touch the hot tube.
